Do not assume unresolved architecture decisions. The repo is the design-system source of truth and Figma is a target. If token source format, component-token layers, target priority, versioning, or generated artifact policy is unclear, ask before changing it.

Prefer canonical sources:

- New token source direction: `tokens/source/`
- Current legacy token build input: `tokens/*_tokens.json`
- Component CSS: `components/css/*.css`
- Component contracts: `components/contracts/*.contract.json`
- Component JS: `components/js/theme.js`
- Manifest: `registry.json`
- Docs pages: `site/src/content/components/*.mdx`

Avoid direct edits to copied/generated outputs unless the task explicitly requires them.

Run `npm run validate:tokens:source` after changing `tokens/source/`. Run `npm run build:tokens:source` and `npm run validate:tokens:source-build` after changing source-token compiler behavior or mode values.

`tokens/source/build/` is an ignored migration/comparison sandbox, not a source directory.

`tokens/source/migration-map.json` must cover every unique legacy token path from `tokens/*_tokens.json`.

`platforms/web/tokens.css` is generated from `tokens/source/` by `npm run build:tokens:web` and is the first real neutral web target. It emits canonical `--tg-*` variables plus compatibility aliases for the existing public component CSS API. `npm run validate:tokens:web-components` verifies that every public `components/css` variable reference is defined.

The neutral web component adapter is generated by `npm run build:adapter:web` into `platforms/web/index.css`, `components.css`, `theme.js`, `adapter.manifest.json`, and `adapter.summary.json`. It is validated by `npm run validate:adapter:web`. The manifest is generated target metadata from registry, contracts, token output, CSS, and JS source facts; do not hand-edit it when source files should change instead.

Shopify tokens are generated from `platforms/web/tokens.css` with `npm run build:tokens:shopify`. Do not edit `platforms/shopify/assets/tokens.css` directly. `npm run build:tokens` remains the legacy Webflow/Framer token build and reads only `tokens/*_tokens.json`.

Shopify adapter assets and manifests are generated by `npm run build:adapter:shopify`. `platforms/shopify/assets/base.css` comes from reset/foundations/utilities source CSS and must not define token values. `platforms/shopify/adapter.manifest.json` and `adapter.summary.json` are generated from registry, contracts, Liquid, section/block schema, data mapping, template composition, CSS, JS source facts, and `shopify-maturity-v1`. Embedded class contracts do not require a dedicated Liquid root. Run `npm run validate:adapter:shopify` after Shopify layout/Liquid/CSS/JS adapter changes.

Shopify target-ready means target-native. Dedicated sections require Liquid plus `{% schema %}` settings, Shopify data mapping, editor support, and JS behavior when the contract needs it. Snippets need stable render parameters and data mapping. Do not treat `config/settings_data.json` as source.

Root-level `*.tokens.json` files are Figma export snapshots for reference/migration, not canonical token sources.

The target architecture has two internal source languages: tokens for values and component contracts for target-agnostic component definitions. Target files are adapters or generated/copy outputs.

The first component contract pilots cover all 183 registry components under `components/contracts/`. Interactive contracts may include target-agnostic `behavior` requirements such as visibility, dismissal, focus management, navigation, motion, form semantics, file handling, validation, submission, commerce formatting, and ARIA semantics. Some generated pilot contracts are conservative and should be refined before code generation. The docs site reads contracts through `site/src/lib/contracts.ts` and renders them with `site/src/components/ContractSummary.tsx`. Run `npm run validate:contracts` after changing contracts, registry component metadata, covered component CSS, or public component tokens.

Accepted directions: DTCG-style `$value`/`$type` tokens, English-first docs, target priority from web to native, generated consumer artifacts published from source, and Shopify target code aligned with theme blocks without deriving sellable work from Horizon.
